THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ADITYA KUMAR MOHAPATRA  ORDER 13.09.2024 Order No.
02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/ Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the materials on record.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with S.T. Case No.94/06 of 2024, arising out of Plantsite P.S. Case No.220 of 2024, pending in the Court of learned Adhoc Additional Sessions Judge (FTSC) (POCSO),
Rourkela, for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 457/380/376 of the I.P.C.
4.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 06.03.2024.
He further contended that in the meantime the investigation has been concluded and final charge sheet has been filed on 30.04.2024.

Further, referring to the allegation made in the F.I.R., learned counsel for the Petitioner contended that the Petitioner has been falsely implicated by the victim, who happens to be the wife of a person who had employed the Petitioner.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that the Petitioner, who was working as a labourer under the husband of the victim, has not been paid his remuneration/wages, as a result of which,
the Petitioner was demanding his legitimate dues.
In turn, the Petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that the case of the Md. Tipu vs State Of Odisha ..... Opposite Party

1 prosecution is highly improbable.
Ffurther, referring to the medical evidence, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the victim was examined by the doctor on the very next date of the occurrence, i.e. 05.03.2024.

The medical examination report of the victim submitted by the concerned Medical Officer on 07.03.2024 clearly reveals that there are no bodily injuries present over the victim, and there are no injuries over the genitals.
Therefore, there are no signs or symptoms of forcible intercourse.
The medical examination report further reveals that there is no physical clue of any alleged sexual offence on the clothes of the victim.
In its entirety, the medical examination report of the victim negates any sexual assault on her as alleged by the victim.
Although the allegation against the present petitioner is not entirely corroborated by the medical examination report.

However, on perusal of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it appears that the victim was sleeping while the alleged occurrence took place and she woke up when the Petitioner was allegedly touching her private parts.

On such grounds, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the prosecution case is false and the Petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case at the instance of the victim and her husband.

5. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that the allegations made in the F.I.R. are grave and serious in nature and that in the meantime charge sheet has been filed which reveals that there exits a prima facie case against the Petitioner.
On such ground, learned counsel for the State submitted that the Petitioner is not entitled to be released on bail.

6. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on careful examination of the case diary, medical examination report and the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., this Court is of the view that the medical examination report does not support the prosecution allegation.
7. Taking into consideration the period of custodial detention of the Petitioner and the fact that the charge sheet has already been filed, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.

8. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter.
The release of the Petitioner shall also be subject to such other terms and conditions that would be imposed by the Court in seisin over the matter.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
9. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra) Judge Debasis Md. Tipu vs State Of Odisha .....
